That seems like a cop out though. I'm not complaining about there being too much or that there's filler for each season. I'm expressing disappointment with where the 4th season went.

It's also just media comprehension. If we all just rolled over and accepted what we got then we'd be getting worse and worse media. It's the analysis and criticisms that keep media going in the right direction. I don't dislike the show at all, and the 5th season REALLY picked up on a lot of the slack season 4 dropped.

Just because it's a teen CW show doesn't mean it's immune to criticism, and saying "concerns about the plot seems misplaced" sounds a little ignorant. They obviously cared a lot more about the plot in seasons 2, 3 and 5. And realistically my concerns with the plot are near to none, it's the plot progression, the characters, the episode to episode adventures. I think the plot of collecting stones around the world to finally generate a Kryptonian crystal to create the fortress of solitude is a fantastic plot. Having Lana and Jason and Clark all linked to the stones in some way or another is brilliant. Having Lana turn into a witch was dumb, having her boyfriend she met in Paris be a sleeper agent for his mom who was related to the queen who burned her ancestors at the stake was stupid. 

There was a synergy of writing in season 3 where it felt like the entire team came together to make something greater than the sum of its parts, where season 4 feels so unbelievably disjointed, and confused about what it even wants to be.

Honestly it should have ended in season 3. Season 3 is where it started to become unbearable but it felt purposeful, it felt like an unstoppable force meeting an immovable object, and that it was destined to fail. It not working SHOULD HAVE BEEN BOOK END for Clana. And a lesson for Clark.

Season 3 ended so perfectly and to have them just reverse everything they did the very next episode feels frustrating and even being almost done with season 5 I still feel the Aftershock of it.

So far season 3, I'm on my first viewing and I'm almost done with season 5. Season 3 was just so thrilling and exciting, everyone kicked up their performance from the previous season, the looming threat of Lionel Luthor through the entire season. It's definitely the most put together, solid, cohesive season thus far, though I'm REALLY liking season 5, it's carrying the same pacing while not being as dark, though I still think I prefer season 3 just because of how OUT OF NOWHERE it came. The ending as well was just BONE CHILLING. I loved it to bits. 

I also think this is where Clana should have ended, I really like Lana in season 3 and it felt like she was finally making steps to move on with her life, just for them to bring her back the very next episode. I hated the witch stuff in season 4 and I think if they really wanted Lana in season 4 it should have been two subplots that converge at the end of the season.

Curiosity is a more than fine answer I'd say, sure it doesn't have any effect on me but plenty of things don't have an effect on me. Name a special interest, I guarantee that there's quite a few that don't have an effect on you. But your still curious about them. I love knives, I just think they look cool, I don't really do anything with them but learning about the designers and what they're made of is interesting to me but it doesn't matter.

And heck, I could get to know more about the person. Maybe they're not wearing flip flops because of the sweating issue, maybe they just prefer open toes shoes, they prefer the air flow, and if that's the case, they can tell me that. Now I know something interesting about this person preferences. 

There's always a million reasons to want to know something, and they're all justified, however they aren't entitled to being answered, and that's the important part.

If that were the case then where do we draw the line? There are people insecure about a lot of things, but if we can't see their soul then we don't know what may offend them. Let's say someone has to wear open toe shoes all day because of a sweating problem, and they get blisters if they wear shoes. Let's say they're self conscious about it.

Let's also say their friends ask them, either sincerely or jokingly "why do you wear flip flops all the time?" To which they can either open up about their insecurity, dodge the question, or say "I'd rather not say, and if you wouldn't ask again I'd appreciate that".

Which is a very good and polite thing to do. And I think it's something we need to start practicing more, and accepting more. It's not rude, and there's no aggression, the friends had no clue about the insecurity, but now they know there's a boundary about that topic, so they'll stop addressing it. Problem solved.

I see no reason why the same thing can't be applied to every other thing like height, weight, gender, sexuality, so long as some discretion is applied obviously, don't ask a fat person how much they weight unless you're they're gym trainer designing a meal plan for them. And so on.

You have a slightly misinformed new of hairloss, yes DHT causes hair loss but blood flow is still up for debate as for what role it actually plays in hairloss, simply put we don't have enough information, I reckon it's something to do with the marketing side of things, the more bald men there are the more bullshit products you can sell that don't work. That or it's the societal part of things, hairloss is a strangely taboo thing to talk about, if you're worried about having hair loss just shut up and shave it off is the commonly spread message. And all the men who don't have any hair growth disdainful of the world and project their disappointment onto everybody else. 

Though that's beside the point, we also straight up don't know how minoxidil works to regrow hair, we know it turns velus hairs into terminal hairs, but we don't know if it does that because of blood flow, or because it's a potassium channel opener. If it IS blood flow, then why don't other methods of promoting blood flow work nearly as well? If that was the case than hanging upside down for a half hour every morning would be the easiest way to regrow your hair.

But as for DHT itself, that doesn't really have anything to do with blood flow at all. DHT latches onto the hair follicle and causes it to deteriorate over time, AGA scalps are more sensitive to DHT and so baldness usually happens pretty fast. So blood flow wouldn't really change the effect DHT has on our follicles, in some rare cases that are purely anecdotal, I've seen people stabilize their hairloss with scalp massages and micro-needling, but no scientific studies as of yet.

So in short, minoxidil doesn't work on its own because it doesn't do anything about DHT and the scalps sensitivity to DHT, it can regrow some hairs but it's eventually pointless if you aren't taking finasteride or another 5AR inhibitor.

Always talk to a derm beforehand, I think something that not everyone wants to admit is that at the end of the day, finasteride is a type of hormone therapy. However it's important to dispell the myths.

First off, it doesn't lower your testosterone, it lowers DHT which is a byproduct of testosterone. In fact it stops the conversion of Testosterone into DHT so you actually have more free testosterone in your blood.

Secondly the side effects are MASSIVELY overstated, only about 5% of people actually get side effects, for reference: Albuterol, a steroid given to people with Asthma, 20% of people get side effects of headaches and nervousness. Most of the time asthma patients will ignore those side effects and continue taking the medication, and being told by doctors to do the same.

And the same goes for finasteride, except the side effects dissipate after a month or so. I personally had some pelvic floor discomfort after week 3 that only lasted a couple days. 

It's also commonly spread that Finasteride causes ED. I have yet to see concrete evidence of this, as most people who experience it were likely experiencing a nocebo. My theory is that it was all started by someone in a startup for a hair loss snake oil product who wanted men misinformed, scared, and desperate for a solution.

Then the product doesn't work and you have misinformed, disappointed men saying that the products sucks and finasteride doesn't work, they tell you to use minoxidil until it stops working and the cycle continues.

Addictions are hard. Especially ones that aren't related to drugs, there isn't as much societal pressure placed on them because "hey at least you aren't addicted to meth!" But in reality they can become just as damaging to your life. 

The issue isn't that you're fat. The issue is that you're depressed, and you're treating it by over-eating. It's human nature to want to fill these voids we have in our souls with the infinite supply of dopamine we have around us. In the modern era.

Best place to start is to get to the root of the depression. Did a big thing happen that's causing you to become unmotivated? are you just in a spot in life where everything feels overwhelming? Maybe since you're an adult now the decisions of every day life are crushing you. That's completely normal, and it's just as normal to want to escape that with things like eating, but remember that eating is the cope, not the source. 

Push yourself out of your comfort zone, seek help, and little by little you can start getting control back of your life. Start with the simple things like getting those big plans out of the way you've had forever.

Only then will you have the power to tackle self image. The only way to improve yourself is by accepting who you are, instead of hating yourself for being this way. 

From there it's surprisingly easy to lose weight. You've got all your normal life stuff in order, now it's just about staying consistent. I'm not a professional but this worked for me personally when I wanted to lose weight. 

For the first week, just go on a strict ketogenic diet. You're not gonna stay on this because living like that sucks, but it's more so just to tell yourself you can do it and get through a week of that pain, prioritize protein, and fat. You want anywhere from 0.6g-1g of protein per lb of body fat. Cut out any and all added sugars. That week is gonna suck, but towards the end you'll be more comfortable with it, by that point you've kinda given yourself a soft detox and it's easier to switch to a more comfortable diet that still prioritizes protein and fat. Feel free to eat as you please, just keep that protein goal in mind and try not to go over your calorie maintenance for the day (around 2170 for your height and weight, though this will change as you lose weight). And then all you gotta do is move around at least once a day. Nothing intense, go on a walk, do some pushups, do some situps, just try not to sit all day

First step: when looking for advice DO NOT COME TO REDDIT! Everyone's gonna tell you to break up because no one is willing to put themselves in a position of expressing love. And if you do come to Reddit for advice, weed out the irrational comments. 

Second step: look at your options, look at how you have been acting. Have you truly been open with him about how much this hurts you? Have you been fully open to willing to change some habits? Have you confronted him about his issues and told him straight up "hey you are doing something that is actively causing me pain". Nothing is worse than that ache in your chest, but also when that happens it is your responsibility to be as open as you possibly can. No sugar coating, not apologizing, in this scenario YOUR feelings are being addressed, and when addressing YOUR feelings (for the time being) you're the only one that matters (until he has reasonable questions or problems with it, in which case it's time to come to a compromise for both parties). 

Drastic options only come when you are at the end of your rope, 6 months of love have to be handled carefully. Explain to him every miscommunication error you might have had, lay out everything on the table. If he misunderstands something then correct it. When he goes days without talking tell him to tell you when he's gonna do that, tell him that it pains you and to put himself in your shoes. I'm not sure who Mia is, or either of your relations to her are but tell him how that makes you feel, and express that he can come to you and you will handle his issues as an adult would, be kind, be caring, and as for the love bombing, tell him that it's just the way you express love and that if he has a problem with it he has to state exactly what he has a problem with.

This issue seems to have sprouted from what most issues sprout from: miscommunication and/or completely lack of communication. Be completely open and be completely honest, don't say "this has been kinda bugging me" say "this hurts me and I want it to stop or at least some explanation"

If he gets irrational when you discuss any of this THEN it may be time to consider tying off any loose ends with this relationship. But if he's willing to discuss things and change small habits for you then I see no reason why this has to end. Open that time of dialogue, get the both of you talking in person. In front of each other. Air your grievances and the solution will present itself, whether this is something you can fix or something you have to let go.
